children: German exports in July retreated for the first time since January, snapping a nascent recovery in foreign trade that has helped drive the country's economic growth in the first half of the year.

Exports declined 0.8% on month in July to 138.2 billion euros, or $160.62 billion, Germany's statistics agency said Tuesday. Because imports declined by a larger 5.7%, the country's trade surplus rose to 21.3 billion euros, from 15.4 billion euros in June.

Goods exports to fellow European Union nations, alongside the U.K. and China, all fell back, but exports to the U.S. jumped almost 20% on month. President Trump announced a fresh 10% tariff on EU goods imports in July, replacing temporary levies imposed in February.

Net exports had contributed to Germany's growing economy in the first two quarters of the year, as the Iran conflict caused supply-chain disruptions for Asian competitors, benefiting manufacturers in Germany. Companies also stockpiled inventory in anticipation of higher costs due to the war.
